overview.summary: High-level principles used to reason about collisions, timelines, and contributing factors without providing operational procedures.
learning_outcomes: Understand basic physics concepts relevant to collisions
Identify scene factors that affect interpretation

core_principles.title: Conservation of Momentum (Conceptual)
core_principles.description: In a closed system, total momentum is conserved; used conceptually to reason about pre/post-impact motion.
limits: Real scenes include energy losses and external forces; calculations must state assumptions.

core_principles.title: Energy Transfer (Conceptual)
core_principles.description: Kinetic energy can convert to deformation, heat, sound, and motion; damage patterns relate to energy dissipation.
limits: Damage is not a simple speedometer; material differences matter.

core_principles.title: Friction & Braking (Conceptual)
core_principles.description: Surface friction and braking influence stopping distance; context must include road condition.
limits: Friction varies widely; do not overclaim precision.

core_principles.title: Human Factors (Conceptual)
core_principles.description: Perception-reaction time, attention, and visibility can influence event sequence.

common_failure_modes: No baseline measurements or fixed reference points (conceptual)

education_case_prompts.title: Two-vehicle intersection collision (fictional)
questions: What documentation would reduce uncertainty most?
What timeline anchors could be corroborated?
